title: Verify cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability values are limited to known enum, Aisle-category cells carry no seatPriceDetails
request_summary: Chain A GetSeatMap response (BAH-RUH 2027-06-10, offer GF161) - enumerated distinct cellCategory/cellAvailability values across all 210 cells (30 rows x 7 columns incl. aisle)
response_summary: cellCategory observed: {Seat:177, Aisle:30, NoSeat:3}; cellAvailability observed (populated cells only): {AvailablePaid:177}; every Aisle cell has cellDetails=null (no seatPriceDetails)
expected: Every cellCategory value in {Seat, Aisle} per SPEC.md §2.7; every cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value in {AvailablePaid, Blocked, Occupied}; Aisle cells carry no seatPriceDetails
actual: cellAvailability stayed within the documented enum (only AvailablePaid observed this round - no Blocked/Occupied cells existed on this far-future date). However, a THIRD cellCategory value not in SPEC.md's documented {Seat, Aisle} pair was observed: NoSeat (3 cells, row 8 columns A/B/E - a bulkhead row with fewer real seats than the standard 3-3 layout). NoSeat cells have a non-null column (unlike Aisle, which has column=null) but cellDetails=null (same as Aisle) - i.e. NoSeat is a third, distinct partition, not a mislabeled Aisle/Seat. Per §8.3 policy for an unconfirmed enum value, this is logged as a new UNKNOWN-resolution/spec-update candidate, not a hard failure - the Aisle-carries-no-pricing assertion itself holds unchanged.
evidence: Full cell scan of chain A's 30-row seatMapDetails (segment GF-GF161-GF161-2027061002-2027061004-O): cats={Seat:177,Aisle:30,NoSeat:3}, avail={AvailablePaid:177}; row 8 = A:NoSeat,B:NoSeat,C:Seat,(aisle),D:Seat,E:NoSeat,F:Seat

title: Verify GetSeatMap sets getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID and Book consumes them as ResponseId/selectedOfferId when SeatMap precedes it
request_summary: GetSeatMap succeeded (4 independent chains, BAH-RUH/BAH-JED/BAH-DMM/BAH-CAI); Book POST api/v2/FlightBooking/Book using GetSeatMap's own responseId/offerId directly, attempted 4 times on 4 fresh offers
response_summary: GetSeatMap: 200 every time. Book: HTTP 500 'Unknown error occured' every time (4/4 attempts) - never returned pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR to the caller
expected: GetSeatMap's offerId/responseId feed Book's ResponseId/selectedOfferId directly; Book returns 200 with pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR
actual: BLOCKED this round by a newly-discovered critical outage: every Book AND Hold call for GulfAir/KSA on ne-3 returned HTTP 500 'Unknown error occured' on first attempt across 6 independent fresh offers (routes BAH-RUH x4, BAH-JED, BAH-DMM, BAH-CAI) and 1 Hold attempt, regardless of payload content (with-seat and no-seat bodies both failed identically) - see the run-level defect finding. This makes it impossible to distinguish this test case's own expected behavior from the outage's generic 500. On 2 of the 4 attempts, a same-offer retry with a different payload confirmed via HTTP 409 'This booking has already been created (609)' that the booking WAS actually created server-side despite the 500 - so GetSeatMap->Book chaining itself likely still works, but this cannot be confirmed from the client side since the success response is never delivered.
evidence: GetSeatMap chain (chainA3): responseId=b15ee450-ad7a-4c9b-84cd-e9eaba08e0ad, offerId captured cleanly. Book attempt: TransactionId 74ec9275-4122-405e-b0a3-ac4f11f00d9d (500). Retry-confirmed silent success on a separate chain (chainA4): TransactionId 5abbff77-0b26-4cfd-9616-ea1925de0a94 (409, 'already created')

field_name: HTTP status code / response body (Book, Hold)
summary: NEW CRITICAL DEFECT (candidate BUG-16): Book and Hold return HTTP 500 on the client-facing response for GulfAir/KSA on every call this round, while the booking is silently created server-side regardless - confirmed twice via a same-offer retry returning HTTP 409 'This booking has already been created (609)'. The 409 error envelope also leaks the live upstream supplier SOAP request in plaintext, including a real apiKey and secretKey.
expected_value: HTTP 200 with pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR on the first successful call; no supplier credentials in any error envelope
impact: Every Book/Hold attempt this round created a real, live booking with NO pnr ever returned to the caller - these bookings cannot be voided/cancelled through this harness since the PNR is unknown, and they will sit un-tracked in the supplier's system. This also silently defeated the intent of every other test case that depends on Book (7 of this round's 10 assigned test cases), since none of them could be evaluated against a real 200 response. Separately, live supplier apiKey/secretKey values were observed in the 409 conflict envelope's OriginalSupplierRequest field - the same class of credential leak as the previously-documented BUG-11, but now reachable on the very first Book/Hold call for this supplier/credential pair, not only via a deliberate duplicate-submission probe.
evidence: 6 independent Book attempts (fresh offers on BAH-RUH x4, BAH-JED, BAH-DMM, BAH-CAI) + 1 Hold attempt (BAH-CAI) all returned HTTP 500 'Unknown error occured' (ErrorCode ServerError) on the FIRST call. A same-offer retry on 2 of those chains (chainA3 with-seat, chainA4 no-seat) returned HTTP 409 'This booking has already been created (609)' - proving the original 500'd call had actually succeeded. TransactionIds: 500s = 74ec9275-4122-405e-b0a3-ac4f11f00d9d, 2b439530-64cc-4def-86c5-47baa83db9b0, e3cd3847-9414-4974-b6ad-093367394fd3, ce71a2fa-da95-4a0c-9790-f6b0b898ee92, 06401362-cd7c-4c32-b539-9326a411c273 (Hold); 409-confirmed-silent-success = b913c432-9973-44d8-9cf8-aa0e5e0bbc6a, 5abbff77-0b26-4cfd-9616-ea1925de0a94. Credential fields observed (redacted here per SPEC.md §7.14 - present in raw form in the 409 response body, not reproduced verbatim in this report).

note: At least 2 real bookings were silently created this round (chain A3 with seat 8F on BAH-RUH 2027-06-10, and chain A4 no-seat on BAH-RUH 2027-06-15) but their pnr was never returned to the caller (Book responded 500 both times) - cannot be voided/cancelled by pnr through this harness. Flag to the platform team: a broader lookup (by TransactionId, or a booking search by passenger name 'Ahmed AlSayed'/date) may be the only way to locate and clean these up.

Up to 4 additional Book attempts (chains A, A2, A5-noseat, A6-noseat) and 1 Hold attempt (BAH-CAI) may also have silently succeeded under the same outage pattern, though not individually reconfirmed via a retry - treat as suspect-created bookings pending the platform team's investigation of the underlying 500 defect.
